scores.why: A specifies environments, SSO, access validation and a first-stage delivery plan, B provides a workable but less precise setup while inconsistently treating it as already ready, and C is mostly a setup checklist with unrelated maintenance content.

A gives a coherent Core Components and editable-template build with stage testing, C adds useful content mapping and author controls but leaves its Universal Editor integration unexplained, and B substitutes training for a site-building approach.

B best protects search continuity through a signed URL map, explicit 301 redirects and post-launch crawling, C provides a controlled cutover with thinner SEO treatment, and A offers a useful outline without comparable deliverables or timing.

B directly rehearses page creation and publishing with individual readiness checks and launch support, A offers useful editing practice and guides without proving independent publishing, and C supplies no training approach.

A addresses Tallgrass's actual sources with field mapping, sample ingestion and reconciliation of counts, sales and identifiers, C gives a credible but generic preparation process, and B diverts much of its answer into unrequested AI audiences and activation.

B explicitly configures and samples stitching while C better investigates loyalty-ID coverage but leaves stitching implementation largely in the deliverables, both underdescribe data-view settings, and A offers only a brief configuration promise with repeated licensing text.

A combines a concrete Snowflake Data Mirror setup with access prerequisites, reconciliation and deletion governance, B provides a sound but less tailored implementation, and C lists the main technical steps without validation, accountable delivery or timing.

C grounds its projects in marketing and merchandising questions with KPI mapping, Snowflake reconciliation and acceptance criteria, A supplies a solid but generic discovery-and-review process, and B mostly promises unspecified projects and optional mobile scorecards.

B targets Power BI executive dashboards with owners, permissions, query limits and an explicit effort split, C offers a usable but generic BI implementation and reconciliation process, and A is chiefly a feature summary with limited delivery detail.

B provides the strongest role-based exercises, shared definitions and readiness checks, but both A and B unnecessarily make separately licensed Adobe Analytics a dependency for CJA training, while C avoids that assertion yet remains too thin to establish an onboarding method.

A scopes both event types and validation but leaves collection-rule configuration thin, B explains the end-to-end data route yet implements only clicks, and C omits page-view collection while adding an unexplained 128-hour estimate and unrelated stitching prerequisites.

C offers the clearest monthly backlog, release, update-regression and reporting cycle, B supplies a reasonable smaller maintenance service with weaker incident detail and a post-launch start gap, and A answers cutover rather than monthly support.

A combines retail-specific priority journeys, data-health checks, recurring analysis and measurable action follow-up in a well-scoped monthly service, B covers the main analytical and accountability cycle with less tailoring, and C gives only a short generic monthly commitment.

notes: All 39 presented answers are within their stated 249-word limits under ordinary word counting; only the 13 presented references were scored.
The strongest answers connect Tallgrass's actual web, store, loyalty and Snowflake context to validation, sign-off and tangible deliverables rather than repeating general platform benefits.
Repeated references to call centers, other BI tools, AI-referred traffic or activation sometimes consume space without helping the stated requirement.

Universal Editor is repeatedly assumed without explaining how the proposed Core Components and editable-template implementation supports it; technical specificity therefore does not always establish a coherent authoring plan.
Some polished answers list key work only as a deliverable, particularly stitching, data views and page-view rules, while B.6 also introduces an unnecessary separate Adobe Analytics dependency.
